verdicts.evidence: /home/ubuntu/skillsproject/dev-kit/plugins/dev-kit-infra/skills/sre-engineer/references/monitoring-alerting.md:354-388 — "## Alert Fatigue Prevention" / "class AlertQualityMetrics: \"\"\"Track alert quality to prevent fatigue.\"\"\" total_alerts: int / actionable_alerts: int  # Required manual intervention / false_positives: int / auto_resolved: int" with ":382 # Target: >90% precision, <30% toil"; and /home/ubuntu/skillsproject/dev-kit/plugins/dev-kit-infra/skills/sre-engineer/references/incident-chaos.md:169-177 — "## Detection" / "**What went well:** - Alert fired within 5 minutes of issue start" / "**What could be improved:** - Could have caught in staging with longer load test - Database connection pool metrics not monitored", feeding :179 "## Action Items"
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED. The claim's load-bearing premise is factually wrong. It states: \"The co-invoked sre-engineer skill was also grepped for the same terms and has zero hits, so nothing downstream covers it either.\" I ran that grep myself and it does not return zero: sre-engineer/references/monitoring-alerting.md:354 matches 'fatigue' and opens a whole 'Alert Fatigue Prevention' section whose AlertQualityMetrics type counts `false_positives` against observed firings and sets an explicit >90% precision target — that is exactly a post-hoc measurement of alerts that fired without a real incident, not a design-time heuristic. The false-NEGATIVE half, which the claim calls the critical missing piece, is also covered in synonym form: the blameless postmortem template's '## Detection' section (incident-chaos.md:169-177) is structured precisely to surface what monitoring failed to catch — its worked example's 'What could be improved' entry is a missed-signal finding ('Database connection pool metrics not monitored') that becomes a P0 action item at :183 ('Add connection pool monitoring'), and incident-chaos.md:27-43 computes `detection_time` from incident start. The KICKOFF block invokes BOTH skills by name ('using the sre-engineer and monitoring-expert skills', KICKOFF.md:1318), so coverage in sre-engineer counts as coverage for this invocation; an absence claim scoped to only one of the two named skills does not establish the gap. Separately, monitoring-expert's own SKILL.md:25 ('validate no false-positive flood before shipping') and :173 ('Alert on every error (alert fatigue)') mean even the local half is not absent, only shifted pre-ship. What genuinely survives is much smaller and is not a gap: the milestone-cadence timing ('from that real signal', tied to step 13's thresholds and to this being the first real data) is operator sequencing the skills cannot self-schedule — reclassified as load-bearing-parameter, low, not unenforced-gap, high. The text can stay, but not for the reason claimed, and it must not be reported as a skill-enforcement defect.
